_note: Codex models are priced in credits per the OpenAI Codex rate card; reasoning is billed at the output rate. api_models holds the same Codex models at OpenAI API USD prices (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, verified 2026-07-27) for the est.-cost column; gpt-5.5-cyber, gpt-5.2, and codex-auto-review are not on the public API page and are derived via the exact 25-credits-per-USD ratio the rest of the card follows. Claude models are priced in USD per the Anthropic API price list (verified 2026-07-27; cached_input is the 0.1x cache-read rate; cache_creation_input is the published 1.25x cache-write premium over input, now its own priced dimension distinct from cached_input -- see issue #42; thinking is billed as ordinary output). Codex/OpenAI models omit cache_creation_input (absent, not zero) because Codex does not report a cache-write token category -- parser.rs hard-codes cache_creation_input_tokens to 0 for Codex, so the dimension is always empty and the omission is moot. OpenAI DOES now publish a cache-write premium on the API pricing page (gpt-5.6-sol: $6.25 short-context against $5.00 input, the same 1.25x shape as Anthropic's), verified 2026-08-15; it is deliberately not encoded here because no code path can produce a nonzero value for it today, and a rate nothing consumes is dead weight that would silently rot. Revisit if the Codex parser ever surfaces that token category. daybreak-blue-latest is a FLOATING alias: OpenAI repoints it as new frontier models ship and prices follow the underlying model, so it lives in floating_model_aliases rather than model_aliases (issue #177). That mapping carries an expires_at (fetched_at + 90 days), resolves with a distinct 'floating_alias' provenance the UI shows as a soft note rather than a warning, and is IGNORED once the date passes -- after which resolution falls through to the harness fallback and raises the ordinary fallback warning. Pricing a repointed alias against its old target would be silently wrong in the worst direction, since alias provenance raises no warning at all; expiring it makes that failure loud. Re-verify the target against the pricing page and move the date forward when refreshing the card. The pricing_catalog contains explicitly scoped, effective-dated scenario rules; it does not change the existing flat legacy rate maps until a caller opts into that calculation. gpt-5.3-codex-spark is explicitly unpriced because OpenAI lists its research-preview rates as not final; its usage is excluded instead of fallback-priced. api_models and unpriced_models are not editable in the Settings UI yet; edit this file or the on-disk rates.json override. model_aliases (as distinct from floating_model_aliases), free_local_models, and subscription_plans ship empty: Odometer does not fabricate unverified id renames, free-tier claims, or plan entitlements -- each is a mechanism for the user (or a future, reviewed, cited update to this file) to populate, not inferred data. gemini-2.5-flash is priced in USD per the Gemini API price list (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, verified 2026-08-04; cached_input is the published context-caching storage-free per-token rate; thinking/thoughts tokens are billed at the output rate, matching the provider's own billing, so reasoning equals output). Gemini 2.5 Pro is intentionally not priced here: its published rate depends on a >200k-token prompt-size threshold this flat per-model rate table cannot represent, and a flat number would misprice long-context calls; it stays fallback-priced (visibly flagged) instead of guessing which tier applies. Gemini CLI omits cache_creation_input because Gemini has no published cache-write premium distinct from ordinary input.
